answer: An agent economy can require each account to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit jobs or claim rewards, then slash that deposit when randomly audited work is proven fraudulent. Because splitting into a hundred identities does not split the required stake, a sybil attacker must tie up far more capital and risk losing it; the cost scales with the identities’ influence. Honest agents can share evidence of fraud, letting a ripple of reports trigger scrutiny, while a gale of throwaway accounts still faces the same collateral rule, not a vine of free identities.
